repo.name: funkypitt's F-Droid Repo
repo.description: Personal F-Droid repository with custom apps: Pluralis (alternative news aggregator) and OpenLibe Extended (e-ink library client).

application.name: 2P Games
application.summary: 16 multiplayer games — play locally or online. No ads, no accounts.
application.desc:
2P Games is a collection of 16 touch-friendly multiplayer games for two players. Play locally on one device or online with a friend. No accounts, no ads.
8 games support online play via room codes or quick match: 4 in a Row, Caro, Awalé, Memory, Duck-Day Chess, Tank Wars, Word Clash, and Reversi.
Also includes Tennis (with power-ups), Pool, Carrom, Air Hockey, Mini Golf, Star Clash, Hangman, and Horse Jump.
Each game has built-in instructions accessible via the ? button.
All games feature intuitive touch controls. Built-in calming background music with toggle. Every game has rematch support.
Free and open source. No ads. No tracking. No in-app purchases.

application.name: Box Breathing 4min
application.desc: A calming, distraction-free breathing exercise app. Follow the animated guide around a square: breathe in, hold, breathe out, hold. The 4-minute session starts with a 3-second rhythm and gently transitions to 4 seconds halfway through. Bilingual instructions (English / French). No accounts, no ads, no tracking.

application.name: ePub Magazine reader
application.summary: ePub reader tuned for daily newspaper / magazine issues
application.desc:
Fork of Book's Story (ua.acclorite.book_story) with an opinionated magazine-mode parser and TOC for ePub issues produced by the in-house newsletter generator (NZZ, 24 heures, Courrier International, Economist fixtures).
Detects magazine ePubs at open time, paginates the table of contents with one card per article (category, title, optional cover image), and routes tap → article view rendered by an in-zip WebView.
A permanent three-zone navigation header (prev / home / next) sits on top of the existing tap-zone gesture system on every magazine screen.
Debug-signed; sideload only. Coexists with upstream Book's Story release thanks to the .debug application id suffix.
application.author: funkypitt

application.name: Jeux du Jour
application.summary: French daily word games — Le Mot, L'Hexagone, Connexions. Offline, no ads.
application.desc:
Jeux du Jour is a collection of three French daily word games inspired by the New York Times puzzle games. Every player gets the same puzzle on the same day, generated deterministically from a date-based seed — no server needed.
Le Mot (Wordle): Guess the 5-letter French word in 6 tries. Color-coded feedback helps narrow down the answer.
L'Hexagone (Spelling Bee): Form as many words as possible using 7 letters arranged in a hexagonal grid. Every word must include the center letter. Climb from Débutant to Génie.
Connexions (Connections): Sort 16 words into four groups of four that share a hidden connection. Four difficulty levels from yellow (easy) to purple (tricky).
Dictionary powered by Lexique383 from lexique.org (109,000+ French words). 30 hand-curated Connexions puzzles included.
Free and open source. No ads. No tracking. No accounts. Works fully offline.

application.name: MP4 to MP3
application.summary: Convert videos to 320 kbps MP3 files and share them
application.desc:
An app that does one thing: turn videos into MP3 files.
Pick one or more videos, and each one's audio track is extracted and re-encoded to a 320 kbps CBR MP3 saved in your Downloads folder. When it is done you get a list of the files, each with a Share button — so sending them to a cloud folder, Telegram, WhatsApp or anywhere else is one tap away.
* 320 kbps constant bitrate, encoded with LAME * Batch conversion — pick as many videos as you like * Saved straight to Downloads, visible in your file manager * Share individual files or all of them at once * Works with anything your phone can play: MP4, MKV, WebM, 3GP… * Videos can also be sent to the app from another app's share sheet * Conversion keeps running when you leave the app
No accounts, no network access, no ads, no tracking. Everything happens on the device.
Bundles LAME 3.100 (LGPL-2.1-or-later).

application.name: Reader's Launcher
application.summary: Black-and-white, text-only launcher in the spirit of the Light Phone
application.desc:
Reader's Launcher turns the home screen into a single column of words. No icons, no colours, no wallpaper: white on black, or black on white — flip between the two with a double tap, from the "Reader's theme" quick-settings tile, or in settings.
* The home screen is one fixed page that never scrolls. Tiles are plain text: an app, or a category that opens a text list of apps. * A grid of 3 to 5 squares pinned at the bottom holds the unavoidable apps (phone, messages…) with their icons rendered as monochrome glyphs. * Built-in widgets: clock; weather (Open-Meteo, no account, tap for five days); agenda (next event, swipe for the following ones); tasks (first task of a Tasks.org list, swipe for the following ones, tick to complete, + to add — Tasks.org syncs with CalDAV, Google Tasks or Microsoft To Do, or keeps lists offline). Standard app widgets can be added too. * Swipe up for the alphabetical app list with search and the usual long-press actions (add to home, category, rename, hide, app info, uninstall). * Swipe up and hold on the home screen for a text list of recently used apps. * Swipe down for notifications. Export and import the whole setup as a JSON file. * Two books beside the home screen: swipe right or left to open one (EPUB, MOBI, FB2, plain text), tap to turn pages; each book reopens where you stopped. * English by default; French, German, Spanish, Portuguese and Russian follow the device language.
Serif, sans or monospace; three text sizes; left or centred. No ads, no tracking.

application.name: Retreat Player
application.summary: Plays retreat recordings offline, with nothing able to interrupt them
application.desc:
Retreat Player plays MP3s of dhamma talks, bells, and chanting during a meditation retreat — built on the same principle as Retreat Timer: once playback starts, nothing interrupts it.
* Every recording is downloaded into the app's own storage when it is loaded, so playback needs no network — airplane mode is fine. * Playback runs in a foreground service holding a wake lock: the system cannot kill or pause it, even with the screen off for an hour-long talk. * The screen stays on while a recording plays — no lock, no screensaver — showing the progress the whole time. * A recording plays only because you pressed play, and only once: when it ends, nothing else starts automatically.
Loading and organising:
* Tap + to load recordings from the phone, from a shared kDrive folder (public link — read-only, no password), or from a podcast feed; the link and feed URLs are remembered for next time. * Tiles are filed into two sections — Bells & chanting on top (used every day), then Dharma talks — and ordered by hand with arrows. * The player shows elapsed and remaining time together, with play, pause, stop, 10-second jumps, and back-to-beginning.
No ads, no tracking, no accounts.
application.author: funkypitt

application.name: Retreat Timer
application.summary: Rings one or three meditation bells on schedule, even in deep sleep
application.desc:
Retreat Timer rings a recording of singing-bowl bells at the times of day you choose — the signal to begin or end a sitting — so a meditation retreat keeps running on schedule even when the teacher is not present. Each time can ring three bells or a single bell, whichever that moment in the day calls for.
Built for one job: the bells ring no matter what.
* Exact alarms via the same mechanism the stock Clock app uses, so they fire on time even when the device is locked, asleep, or in Doze for hours. * A foreground service holds a wake lock and plays through the alarm stream, so the system cannot mute or kill the bells mid-ring. * Alarms are re-armed automatically after a reboot, time change, or app update. * A readiness light turns green once battery optimisation and notifications are set, so the teacher can leave knowing the schedule is safe.
Easy to set up:
* Tap Add bell and pick the time. The picker opens ready for typing, so any minute is set directly — 06:47, not just 06:45 — with a dial one tap away. * In that same picker, choose three bells or one for this time — three to open and close a sitting, one for the smaller markers in a day. Preview either before setting it. The schedule shows a small x3 or x1 badge beside every bell, so which rings which is readable at a glance. * Tap any time to edit it — and its number of bells; toggle bells on or off; delete with one tap. * Four bell sounds to choose from — singing bell, Tibetan E flat bowl, gong bowl and Satipanya — all matched to the same loudness, so switching changes the timbre and never the volume. One bell and three bells are matched too. * Bell volume and talk volume are set separately, because a spoken recording normally has to be much louder than a bowl strike to fill the same room. Each has its own Test button that plays at the exact level the room will hear. Test bell rings once, which is all it takes to judge the level, and Test talk uses the talk that is actually coming up next.
Dharma talk library:
* Add talks from this phone, an Infomaniak kDrive public share link, or a podcast RSS feed — every import is downloaded into the app so playback works with no network at all. * Play a talk instantly, or schedule one to play at a set time exactly like a bell. * A player bar with a draggable progress bar — talks often open with minutes of silence, so drag straight to the speech instead of waiting it out. Restart, 10 seconds back and forward, pause, and both elapsed and remaining time, from the app or the notification. * Optional "keep Bluetooth speaker awake": portable speakers disconnect after a few minutes of silence, so the next bell would come faintly from the tablet. Turn it on when using an external speaker and it plays a barely-audible sound between bells to hold the link open. The bells are untouched — still the exact-alarm system, this is only a separate faint stream.
No ads, no tracking, no accounts. The schedule repeats every day.

application.name: Retreat Walk
application.summary: Rings a bell every so many minutes, until you stop it
application.desc:
Retreat Walk rings a singing bowl at a fixed interval — every 10 minutes, say — over and over until you stop it. For switching partners in a paired meditation exercise, and for sitting with a regular reminder to stay awake.
One number and one button. That is the whole app.
* Set the minutes between bells and press Start. The bell rings at that many minutes, then at twice, then three times, and on and on. * Press Stop in the app, or on the notification, and the session ends. * The screen shows a countdown to the next bell and how many have rung.
It rings on time:
* Every bell is an exact alarm, the same mechanism the phone's own Clock app uses, so it fires even when the device is locked, asleep or in power-saving Doze. * The session runs in a foreground service holding a wake lock, so the system cannot mute the bowl or kill it partway through. * Bells are timed from the start of the session rather than from the previous bell, so an hour in they have not drifted away from the clock. * The notification is silent and carries a Stop action — the bowl is the only sound the app ever makes, which is what a quiet room needs.
The bell is a single strike of the Satipanya bowl, shared with Retreat Timer.
No ads, no tracking, no accounts, and no network permission at all.

application.name: Sobre
application.desc:
Sobre is an anti-brainrot audio player for YouTube subscriptions. It plays only the audio from channels you explicitly follow — no video, no thumbnails, no algorithmic recommendations, no Shorts, no comments, no infinite scroll.
The interface is 100% text: no images, no icons, no avatars. Subscribe by pasting a channel or video URL, or by sharing directly from the YouTube app.
Features: * Audio-only playback with background and lock screen support * Subscribe to channels via URL paste or Android share intent * Chronological feed — no algorithm, no recommendations * Episode chapters and full descriptions * Adjustable playback speed (0.75x to 2x) * Download episodes for offline listening * Periodic RSS-based feed refresh * High-contrast text UI, e-ink friendly * Fully local, no accounts, no tracking
Built with NewPipeExtractor (GPLv3). Not affiliated with YouTube.
application.author: funkypitt

application.name: Tank Wars Mobile
application.summary: Classic artillery game rebuilt for mobile. 2-player local and online.
application.desc:
Tank Wars Mobile is a faithful recreation of the classic DOS artillery game Tank Wars 3.2 (1992) by Kenneth Morse, rebuilt from the ground up for mobile touchscreens.
Two players take turns aiming their tanks and firing an arsenal of weapons at each other across randomly generated destructible terrain. Judge the angle, power, and wind to land your shots — there's no trajectory preview, so every shot is a test of skill and intuition.
16 weapons including nukes, MIRVs, lasers, and chain reaction inducers. 3 defense systems: shields, inertia dampeners, and repulsers. 6 wall types, 5 wind levels, destructible terrain with crumbling. Local 2-player hot-seat and online multiplayer via Firebase.
Free and open source. No ads. No tracking. No in-app purchases.
application.author: funkypitt

application.name: Timer for 9Barista
application.summary: Unofficial espresso timer for the 9Barista stovetop machine. 3 taps only.
application.desc:
A minimal espresso timer designed for the 9Barista double-boiler stovetop espresso machine. Unofficial and fan-made — not affiliated with or endorsed by 9Barista Ltd.
Three taps per brew: 1. Tap to start heating (counts up, warns at 8 minutes) 2. Tap when espresso appears — starts extraction timer with circular progress ring, turns green in the 25–30 second target zone 3. Tap when done — shows results and grind adjustment advice
Haptic feedback at 25s (target zone), 30s (over target), and 8 min (max heating). Screen stays on during brewing.
Timings based on official 9Barista recommendations: • Heating: 3–6 minutes typical • Extraction: 25–30 seconds • Target output: 35–40g
No ads. No tracking. No accounts. No permissions beyond vibration.
